Former Commonwealth and British boxing champion, Peter Oboh, who is now a minister of God, has urged Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, to ensure the removal of faeces and other human waste from the Oshodi-Apapa Expressway.
Oboh described the situation as a serious public health concern, warning that poor sanitation could worsen the spread of diseases such as Ebola if an outbreak occurred in the state.
In a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Monday, he lamented that the Oshodi-Apapa Expressway had been turned into a toilet and waste dump by residents.
The statement read, “Your Excellency, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, there is a big issue that is worse than, and can escalate, Ebola. This very big issue is the Oshodi-Apapa Expressway. Right from Cele, through Ijesha all the way to Mile 2 and into the ports – the median is covered in faeces and other human waste.
“This, my dear governor, is worse than Ebola for now. It is very sad to see that the Apapa-Oshodi Expressway has been turned to a toilet and waste bin by residents. Also, one needs to ask what the drivers’ unions are doing about motor boys and tanker drivers who add to this filth?
“I have travelled all over the world, but I have not seen any sight as bad as what is happening on the Oshodi-Apapa Expressway. Please, Mr Governor, you must apply an iron fist to stop this disaster before your tenure expires in a few months. Lagos is too vital not to be kept clean.
“All round, Nigeria is blessed. I can see everything turning around for our good. But quick action is needed to expel the wicked one among us over this evil and shameful activity inspired by a demonic mindset. My beloved Lagos city can be cleaned for good.”
